metaTitle: Link Building: What It Is and What It Costs
metaDescription: Link building is earning links from other sites on purpose. Here are the tactics that still work in India, the rupee ranges, and the ones that backfire.
definition: Link building is the deliberate practice of getting other websites to link to yours, in order to improve how search engines judge your site's authority.
answer: Link building is getting other websites to link to yours on purpose. The tactics that survive Google's spam policies are digital PR, original data, expert commentary and genuine partnerships. In India, marketplace placements are pitched at ₹2,000–₹25,000 each and mostly buy nothing; earned links cost more in time and actually count.
takeaways: A ₹2,000 directory listing does nothing for rankings, has done nothing for over a decade, and is still the most-sold product in the Indian link market.
Google's December 2022 link spam update leaned toward **neutralising** unnatural links rather than penalising sites. Your money disappears quietly instead of loudly.
A serious campaign lands a handful of relevant referring domains a month, not thirty.
Price the proposal, not the promise. Divide the monthly link budget by the links promised and see what one is supposedly costing.

body: Every link you didn't ask for was earned by something: a page worth citing, data nobody else published, a quote a journalist needed at 4pm. Link building is making that happen deliberately rather than waiting.

In an agency it's three jobs on one invoice line: finding targets, creating the reason to link — the expensive part, and the part most agencies skip — and outreach, which is mostly rejection. If a method would be embarrassing to describe to the person who runs the linking site, it's a purchase with extra steps.

body: These are ranges we see quoted here — in agency proposals, marketplace outreach and the offers landing in founders' inboxes. Market observation, not survey data, and they move constantly. Use them to sanity-check a quote, not as a price list.

callout.title: Do the division
callout.body: If a retainer allocates ₹20,000 a month to links and promises fifteen of them, that's ₹1,333 per link. Nothing that costs ₹1,333 was earned. Full ranges and how retainers split are in [what link building costs](/cost/link-building-cost).

sections.h2: Link schemes, and the penalty that isn't a penalty
body: Google's spam policies define link schemes plainly: buying or selling links that pass ranking credit, excessive exchanges, large-scale article campaigns with keyword-rich anchors, automated link creation. Most of the Indian link market sits inside that definition, which everyone involved knows.

Two things can happen. A **manual action** — a human reviewer flags unnatural links, a message appears in Search Console, rankings drop, and recovery needs a clean-up plus a reconsideration request. Far more common is **neutralisation**: the spam systems simply stop counting the links. No message, no drop, no signal at all. Founders brace for the first and get the second, which is commercially worse — a penalty at least tells you to stop.

sections.h2: How many links a real campaign lands
body: Work the arithmetic and the promises collapse on their own. One genuine placement needs research, something worth pitching, two follow-ups and often a piece of writing — several hours per landed link, at a hit rate frequently below one in ten.

At a link budget of ₹20,000–₹30,000 a month, which is what a ₹75,000 SEO retainer can sensibly allocate, a competent team earns between two and eight relevant referring domains a month. It's a range because sector decides it: fintech and healthcare journalists take commentary readily, industrial manufacturing doesn't.

Two to eight looks weak beside a marketplace offering thirty, and compounds differently. Eight relevant domains a month for a year is a profile; 360 purchased placements is an audit finding. Our [link building work](/services/link-building-services) runs at the first pace, which is part of why we take three clients a month.

sections.h2: Four questions to ask before you sign
body: Ask these in the pitch and watch how long the answers take. An agency that earns links answers all four in under a minute.
numbered: **"Show me the last ten links you built for a client in my sector."** Not a portfolio — ten live URLs. Then check whether those sites have traffic.
**"Do you pay for placements, and do those links carry `rel="sponsored"`?"** There's a correct answer and a revealing one.
**"What's the monthly link budget, and how many links does it buy?"** Then divide.
**"What's the reporting?"** Live URLs, anchor text, follow status, first-seen date. Not a count — a count is what you report when the URLs won't survive inspection.

callout.title: "Our network"
callout.body: An agency describing its link sources as a private network, a partner network or premium inventory is describing a private blog network. That's a link scheme by Google's own definition, and your domain carries the risk, not theirs.

faqs.q: How much does link building cost in India?
faqs.a: Marketplace placements get pitched at ₹2,000–₹25,000 each and mostly do nothing. Genuine earned links cost agency time rather than a placement fee, which typically works out far higher per link — and that's the point. Budget by month, not by link, and expect a handful of real domains rather than dozens.

faqs.q: Is link building still worth it in 2026?
faqs.a: On competitive commercial queries, yes — when several sites have equally good pages, links often decide the order. On long-tail and low-competition terms, content and technical health do the work and a link budget is wasted. Fix the site and the pages first, then buy attention for the best of them.

faqs.q: What is white hat link building?
faqs.a: Earning links by giving people a reason to link: original data, useful tools, expert commentary, genuine partnerships, and correcting unlinked mentions of your brand. The test is simple — if you'd be comfortable explaining the method to the editor of the linking site, it's on the right side of the line.

faqs.q: How do SEO agencies get backlinks?
faqs.a: The honest ones run digital PR, publish data worth citing, place expert commentary with journalists, and reclaim unlinked mentions. The rest buy guest posts on marketplaces and report the count. You can tell which is which in one question: ask for ten live URLs from a recent client.
